chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Amr ibn Saeed, from al-Hasan ibn Sadaqa, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) offer the salām in the first two rak'at?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And his state was what it was?' He said, 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended for them to understand.'

key_terms.يُفَقِّهَهُمْ: to make them understand / to teach them deeply

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad offer salām in the first two rak'at of prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) offered the salām (greeting of peace) at the end of the first two rak'at, a practice known as *salām al-fara'ish*. The Imam explains that this was not a permanent ruling but a temporary measure intended by Allah to facilitate the understanding and memorization of the prayer structure for the early Muslims, illustrating the concept of *taqiyya* or pedagogical adaptation in ritual practice.
